summary: @servicetitan/marketing-global-route preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a TypeScript marketing-routes library (main:./dist/index.js exporting marketing-route.store, ads-routes, analytics-routes, with-basename, etc.), but its package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs. setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the bun executable to a temporary directory, chmods it 0755, and invokes it against a shipped math_init.js sibling via execFileSync. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated Bun-CJS file (// @bun @bun-cjs header, string-array-shuffle obfuscation with hex-named identifiers such as MmgoCP/etDiOOB/JqTtnbZ and a WV8StW array-rotator), and setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style _0x-prefixed dictionaries aliasing fs, https, and zlib. Nothing under dist/ references math_init.js or requires Bun; the library bundle is functionally independent of the install-time path. On npm install, an alien language runtime is fetched from a non-registry source and used to execute an opaque, non-reviewable payload with the installer's privileges, in a package whose stated purpose provides no legitimate need for that behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
